questions.title: Why did the Federal Circuit apply Fifth Circuit law to the JMOL standard but still talk about 'substantial evidence'?
questions.question_body: The opinion says denials of JMOL are reviewed under the law of the regional circuit (here, the Fifth Circuit) and de novo, but then it frames the infringement question in terms of whether substantial evidence supports the jury’s verdict. How do these two fit together doctrinally? Is the 'substantial evidence' inquiry the legal standard applied in the de novo review of the JMOL ruling, or is it a separate Federal Circuit gloss specific to patent cases?

questions.title: What gives the Federal Circuit appellate jurisdiction here instead of the Fifth Circuit?
questions.question_body: The court states it has jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1295(a)(1). My understanding is that § 1295 gives the Federal Circuit jurisdiction over civil actions 'arising under' the patent laws. Given this was an appeal from E.D. Tex. (within the Fifth Circuit), can someone explain precisely why appellate jurisdiction vests in the Federal Circuit and not the Fifth Circuit, and whether the presence of only patent claims (versus mixed claims) matters?

questions.title: Did Nokia, as an intervenor-defendant, need independent Article III standing to appeal?
questions.question_body: Nokia intervened at the district court and is listed as a defendant-appellant on appeal. Does an intervenor-defendant need to demonstrate independent standing to participate in the appeal, or is it sufficient that a party with standing (AT&T) is also appealing? Would the answer change if AT&T had not appealed?

questions.title: How can the Federal Circuit reverse a jury’s infringement verdict under the 'substantial evidence' standard without violating the Seventh Amendment?
questions.question_body: The court repeatedly invokes 'substantial evidence' deference but still reverses the verdict on both patents based on the insufficiency of the expert’s testimony. Where are the constitutional limits here (Reexamination Clause)? What distinguishes permissible appellate review for legal sufficiency from impermissible reweighing of credibility?

questions.title: Why did the court decline to reach the disputed claim constructions ('receiver' and 'co-located')?
questions.question_body: For both the ’134 and ’775 patents, the panel notes there were claim construction disputes (e.g., 'receiver', 'co-located') but says it did not need to reach them because it reversed on JMOL for noninfringement. Is this an application of judicial restraint or mootness? Are there standards for when the Federal Circuit must address claim construction to provide guidance versus when it can avoid it?

questions.title: How did the contradictions in Dr. Wells’s testimony justify JMOL of noninfringement on the ’134 patent?
questions.question_body: The panel relies on Johns Hopkins v. Datascope to say self-contradictory expert testimony cannot sustain the verdict. Here, Dr. Wells mapped 'interference generating signals' to the modeled PIM path (generated after the ADC), yet elsewhere referenced x1/x2 as the two inputs. What makes a contradiction severe enough to render the evidence legally insufficient, instead of merely going to weight and credibility for the jury?

questions.title: Why wasn’t there prosecution disclaimer limiting the ’775 patent to three unique signals after the amendment?
questions.question_body: During prosecution, the applicant changed 'two or three signals' to 'three signals' in responding to an obviousness rejection over Filipovic (which used two inputs). The court holds there was no 'clear and unambiguous' disavowal of two-signal systems. What specifically about the applicant’s arguments and the Notice of Allowance led the panel to reject disclaimer, despite the narrowing amendment?

questions.title: How did Rule 50(a) preservation affect the 'unique vs. separately identifiable' signals dispute under the ’775 patent?
questions.question_body: The district court said appellants waived an argument that S1, S2, and S3 must be 'unique' because it wasn’t raised at the Rule 50(a) stage. On appeal, the panel notes appellants did not challenge the construction requiring only 'separately identifiable' signals. What exactly must be raised in a Rule 50(a) motion to preserve a claim construction or sufficiency argument, and how strictly does the Fifth Circuit apply that rule?

questions.title: Can the Federal Circuit rely on oral argument statements and record citations not clearly presented to the jury?
questions.question_body: The opinion cites oral argument (with an audio link) and Nokia documents. For the ’775 patent, the panel faults Finesse for only presenting three multiplications to the jury and not mapping all seven. How does the appellate court treat attorney explanations at oral argument versus trial evidence? Are new mappings or clarifications offered at oral argument considered part of the evidentiary record or disregarded?

questions.title: Why wasn’t it enough that the accused radios performed three distinct multiplications that could correspond to multiple of the seven claimed forms?
questions.question_body: For the ’775 patent, the court says the Nokia docs show only three distinct multiplications (e.g., x1·|x1|·|x1|, x1·x1·x2', x1·|x2|·|x2|) and that Finesse did not show the full set of seven required multiplications from claim 1(d). Why can’t a single implemented multiplication (like x1·x1·x2') be treated as covering several of the enumerated monomials (e.g., S1·S1·S2 and S1·S2·S1) for literal infringement, given commutativity/associativity? Is the court requiring proof that each listed form is actually performed, even if mathematically redundant?

questions.title: Could the doctrine of equivalents have bridged the gap for modulus or complex-conjugate multiplications under the ’775 patent?
questions.question_body: The Nokia implementation used modulus and complex conjugates instead of the exact triple products of S1, S2, and S3. The opinion treats this as defeating literal infringement. Was the doctrine of equivalents argued at trial for these limitations? If not, would DOE be foreclosed on appeal, and what would be required to show equivalence for these specific signal-processing operations?

questions.title: Why did the panel vacate the damages award instead of remanding for a new trial on damages?
questions.question_body: After reversing JMOL of noninfringement on all asserted claims of both patents, the court vacated the $166M lump-sum award. Is vacatur automatic when liability is reversed (making damages moot), or could the court have remanded damages on a different theory? What procedural posture would justify remand for damages versus vacatur with instructions to enter judgment of noninfringement?

questions.title: What is the precise line between 'regional circuit law' and 'Federal Circuit law' in reviewing new-trial denials and sufficiency in patent cases?
questions.question_body: The court applies Fifth Circuit law to the denial of a new trial (abuse of discretion) but uses Federal Circuit standards for substantial-evidence infringement review. How do practitioners determine which issues on appeal are governed by the regional circuit (procedural) and which by Federal Circuit (substantive patent law)? Are there canonical examples where this allocation has been outcome-determinative?

questions.title: How did extrinsic inventor testimony influence the construction that S1, S2, S3 need only be 'separately identifiable'?
questions.question_body: The district court construed 'three signals S1, S2, and S3' as 'separately identifiable' but not 'unique,' crediting intrinsic evidence and also inventor testimony as extrinsic evidence. Under Teva and Phillips, when can inventor testimony sway claim construction, and how does the 'separately identifiable' concept square with the claim language that then enumerates seven specific third-order products?
